item.title: Renting vs Buying: How to Decide in 2026
item.description:
Introduction

The renting versus buying question is usually argued as though one answer is correct in general. It is not. The right answer depends on how long you stay, what housing costs in the city you are moving to, and how much of your savings you are willing to keep illiquid.

In 2026 the calculation is more sensitive than it has been in recent years, because mortgage rates, home prices, and rents have not moved together. Treating the decision as a comparison of monthly payments alone produces the wrong answer often enough to be expensive.

item.title: How to Calculate the True Cost of Moving to a New City
item.description:
Introduction

Moving to a new city involves more than just comparing rent prices. The true cost of relocation includes dozens of factors that can add thousands of dollars to your expenses — or save you money you didn’t know about.

The Big Picture

When considering a move, most people look at:

  • Rent or mortgage payments
  • Utilities
  • Groceries

But the true cost includes:

  • Moving expenses (truck, packing, insurance)
  • Security deposits and first month’s rent
  • Utility setup fees
  • Vehicle registration and insurance changes
  • Income tax differences
  • Healthcare network changes
  • Professional licensing transfers
  • Cost to replace items you sell/donate

item.title: Understanding Walkability: Why It Matters for Your Next Move
item.description:
Introduction

Walkability isn’t just a buzzword — it’s one of the most important factors in quality of life that most people overlook when choosing a city.

What Is Walkability?

Walkability measures how easy it is to live daily life without a car. The EPA’s National Walkability Index scores neighborhoods from 1 (car-dependent) to 20 (walker’s paradise).

Why Walkability Matters

Financial Benefits

  • Average household in walkable neighborhood saves $10,000+ annually on transportation
  • Higher property values (5–15% premium)
  • Lower healthcare costs

Health Benefits

  • 45 minutes more daily physical activity
  • Lower obesity rates
  • Reduced risk of heart disease and diabetes

Environmental Benefits

  • 30% lower carbon footprint
  • Reduced air pollution
  • Less urban heat island effect

How to Find Walkable Neighborhoods

  1. Check our city pages for walkability scores
  2. Look for mixed-use zoning
  3. Check proximity to grocery stores, pharmacies, and parks
  4. Evaluate public transit connections
